messages:
nikita rao: quick heads up - onboarding sampleapp started getting sporadic 429s and double-billing-looking inflight counts after we turned on the cursor-pool optimization last night

olivia chen: cursor-pool? that's the change to reuse pagination cursors across sessions to avoid warmups, right?

nikita rao: yep. goal was to keep warm cursors hot. but looks like when a pooled cursor is returned while its original owner is still inflight we end up counting it twice in the client semaphore

samir patel: can you paste a tiny sanitized log snippet? curious how the limiter sees it

nikita rao: logs (sanitized):\n```
[2026-11-02T02:15:01Z] cursor-pool: checkout cursor=cur-42 owner=user-A
[2026-11-02T02:15:01Z] prefetcher(user-B): start cursor=cur-42 inflight=9 limit=8
[2026-11-02T02:15:01Z] http GET /v1/paginate status=200 cursor=cur-42 owner=user-B
[2026-11-02T02:15:01Z] user-A: continue req=req-17 inflight=10 limit=9 -> 429
```
\nolivia chen: oh. pool returned cur-42 to user-B while user-A still had it logically reserved. the inflight accounting is per-cursor id, not per-owner, so it gets double-counted when both sides increment

samir patel: repro is easy: start N concurrent cursors owned by different users, then return them to pool immediately and re-checkout from other workers. pool path doesn't check owner or active marker before handing out.

nikita rao: short-term mitigation: disabling cursor-pool in sampleapp config and rolling back the optimization. I'll flip it in staging now

deploy-bot: canary deploy requested: cursor_pool_enabled=false to sampleapp-staging by @nikita rao

olivia chen: long-term fixes we discussed: 1) namespace pool by user/tenant (cheap, no surprise) OR 2) add an owner-check and an in-use flag with compare-and-swap so a cursor isn't reissued until it's fully released OR 3) switch to ephemeral lightweight cursors and keep pool only for truly idle ones

samir patel: my preference: owner-namespace + a short TTL before reuse (like 2s) so transient overlap won't leak counts. also add a client-side invariant check that refuses to hand out a cursor if semaphore count shows it still in use

nikita rao: i'll open a small PR with two things: disable-by-default pool config + owner-namespace and TTL. also adding a unit test that simulates cross-user checkout race

samir patel: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/1027 (WIP) - adds owner namespacing + tests

olivia chen: thanks. adding a note to onboarding doc: "If you enable cursor pooling and see unexpected 429s, disable pool or reduce pool reuse TTL until patch lands."

leo.bot: reaction :eyes: from 2 users

nikita rao: staging looks stable after disable. will keep monitoring and post metrics in next 15m

samir patel: filing an SDK parity issue to ensure other language SDKs either don't share cursor pools across tenants or have the same owner checks

nikita rao: nice catch by monitoring. small change but nasty UX when it hits concurrency windows :thumbsup:
